banks.detail: October-29 hold virtually certain — Reuters Oct-8 poll: 70 of 73 economists expect a hold at 2.50% (markets had priced only ~11.7% Oct hike chance). December hike ~88% (64/73 economists; money markets ~35bp by year-end, i.e. one hike plus partial chance of two; terminal seen at 3.00% by a third). German PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%); EZ final CPI 3.8% confirmed. France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); 2,828 of 3,396 amendments unexamined; OAT-Bund ~157-160bp Wednesday (widest since the 2009-11 crisis); OAT 10Y 5.00% (first since Jul 2002). Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 negative — markets expect a one-notch cut to A1). Lagarde: the fix 'lies at home in France.'
banks.summary: The ECB is expected to hold in October and is leaning toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

banks.detail: October 29-30 a hold — 'virtually no chance' of an October hike (InvestingLive, Oct 21); Reuters Oct 20 (four BoJ sources): the bank may upgrade its inflation forecast and hold steady. December hike ~73-74% (InvestingLive, Oct 21; Reuters poll: 69% expect a Q4 hike, ~80% of those picking December; 60% see 1.75% by end-June 2027). Ueda's 'quite close' to 2% leans December, not October. Japan's 20Y JGB auction saw strongest demand on record. Sep trade deficit -¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn fc (exports +16.7% missed +20.1%). USD/JPY 158.0-158.3 Wednesday morning.
banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December rather than October. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen.

banks.detail: November-5 hike ~96-98% to 4.00% (LSEG via Reuters: 'nearly fully pricing in' post-CPI; AJ Bell: 'nearing 100%'). UK Sep CPI 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst — highest since Oct 2025, energy/motor fuels the driver; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky; PPI +4.6% vs 4.3%) — reinforces the priced path: GBP/USD +0.1% to ~1.339 post-print, EUR/GBP 83.80p strongest in 17 months. December back-to-back ~61% pre-CPI; post-CPI AJ Bell sees '>50% chance' of a year-end second hike. UK labor beat stands: unemp 4.7% (lowest since mid-2025), wages 3.7%. Greene hawkish: wage disinflation 'has stalled at levels above those consistent with inflation at 2%.' ING: BoE to hike Nov + Feb, then pause. LSEG: four hikes priced by mid-2027; Pantheon: Nov + Feb, "very close to adding a third in May." Healey's first Budget Oct 28.
banks.summary: The Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5, and the debate is already about December. This week's UK jobs and inflation data will shape how far it goes.
